transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-29
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (scheduled)
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Tom Hayes (OrionWorks Eng Lead), Priya Nair (OrionWorks SRE), Ethan Cole (OrionWorks PM)

Auto-summary: Quick walkthrough of Console tracing, request-forensics and playback; demo of KV cache fallbacks and tracing correlation; discussed security/architecture for private pilot.

[00:00] Samir (Redwood): hey team thanks for joining, really appreciate you fitting us in. quick agenda: show console trace flows, request playback, KV cache diagnostics, and then talk pilot next steps. any additions?
[00:12] Tom (OrionWorks): no that sounds good. major thing for us is we see intermittent 500s and flakiness on long-context prompts, so want to see how we can triage and where costs are going, yeah.
[00:25] Lena (Redwood): got it, we'll zoom into a failing request path, show how timestamps and token-level latency look, and then demo replay to reproduce. i'll probably use one of your anonymized traces if you shared earlier — if not i'll use a synthetic fail to show the flow.
[00:40] Priya (OrionWorks): we did upload two traces to the folder, but they might have some PII, we redacted but not sure about the format.
[00:48] Samir: perfect we can ingest those, lena will show the mapping, and on the security side we've got SOC2 docs and KMS integration notes which i'll send after.
[00:58] --- demo start ---
[01:12] Lena: ok jumping into the Console — apologies if the screen is a bit choppy — i'm on the request inspector. here's the top-level trace view, you'll see request id, model variant, region, and a timeline with spans. note the orange bands, that's where we saw elevated generate_time and waiting on kv cache fetches.
[01:35] Tom: are the orange bands indicating CPU contention or network?
[01:39] Lena: it's token generation latency; the span label shows "kv_cache_lookup" which points to cache miss and fallback to full context regen. sometimes the transcription engine (uh, i mean inference runtime) will do a chunked fetch; note the duration here is ~320ms for a single lookup which is higher than our P90 for this model.
[01:58] Priya: hm 320ms per lookup is brutal when you have many prefixes. we suspected our prompt stitching caused multiple KV entries. is the console able to show the matched cache key?
[02:08] Lena: yes — there's a metadata pane. sometimes keys get hashed differently if prompt templating changes. you can see the raw key and the hashed id. keep in mind the console obfuscates user content for privacy in hosted mode — but in private mode you'd see full keys if you opt in.
[02:30] Ethan: quick question — can we set alerts on repeated kv cache misses? we'd want to prevent cost spikes.
[02:35] Samir: yeah, alerting and SLO hooks are in Console -> Alerts. You can tie it to "kv_miss_rate" and configure a runbook to automatically reroute to a cheaper model or increase batch size.
[02:50] Lena: ok now i'll show request replay. i'm selecting the failed request, hit 'replay', we can replay locally or to a dedicated sandbox. i'm going to replay to a sandbox set to the same model and token limits.
[03:05] [03:05] Lena: reproducing... you'll see the timeline, and then the output — same 500 pattern appears after 2.1s at the same token boundary. this helps us narrow whether it's input preprocessing vs runtime.
[03:24] Tom: that's super helpful. currently our stack is self-hosted on k8s, but we're exploring Redwood Dedicated. can the replay target our on-prem environment?
[03:34] Lena: we support routing via the private plane to your VPC for Dedicated/Private deployments. for replay, we can either run a synthetic against a pinned model variant on Redwood or provide an off-ramp to run the replay harness within your environment (you'd need the replay-agent container).
[03:51] Priya: what's in that replay-agent — does it store tokens locally? any encryption?
[03:58] Lena: good question. the replay-agent streams only the minimal metadata unless you enable full payload mode. when enabled, payloads are encrypted with your KMS key; we never store plaintext forever — retention policies apply per pilot contract. i'll attach the replay-agent readme.
[04:18] Samir: note on compliance: we've got SOC2 type II, we can do data residency in certain regions, and for Private deployments we can integrate with customer KMS or HSM. i'll include the network diagram.
[04:30] Ethan: on SLOs — our product wants P95 inference latency under 300ms for short prompts and 1.5s for long context at 99% availability. is that feasible?
[04:42] Lena: it's feasible with Dedicated capacity and tuned batching. the Console's telemetry will show latency distribution and the per-token breakdown. one important lever is prefix caching — when prefix hit rate is high, effective latency drops a lot. if you see oscillating hit rates we can recommend prompt normalization to increase hit rate.
[04:58] Tom: are there any automatic normalization helpers in the Console? like to detect near-duplicate prefixes causing cache churn?
[05:05] Lena: we have an "Optimize" suggestions tab — it will flag high-variance tokens and suggest normalization rules (strip whitespace, canonicalize dates, etc.). it's heuristics based but helps.
[05:18] --- mid-demo interjection ---
[05:22] Priya: i noticed earlier you mentioned fallback policies — can we prefer cheaper model fallback for non-critical tokens?
[05:27] Samir: yes, routing policies let you set per-route fallbacks (e.g., if latency > 800ms, route to half-precision quantized model). you can also set a canary for A/B testing.
[05:38] Lena: i'll show the route policy editor — here's a canary with a warmup and automatic rollback if quality drops. the Console surfaces quality metrics tied to prompt-eval suites so you can see BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics or custom prompts failing.
[05:58] Tom: ok if we detect a regression during a canary, can the system auto-fallback to previous model?
[06:03] Lena: yes, there's an automatic fallback/rollback toggle and a threshold. you can also choose manual intervention.
[06:10] Ethan: curious about cost telemetry — can we get token-level cost per route?
[06:15] Samir: absolutely, the Cost tab breaks down token cost by route, by model, and by day. for pilots we can surface estimated monthly cost.
[06:25] Lena: switching back to the trace — here's a deep span that shows repeated serialize/deserialize steps on the runtime, likely coming from a library mismatch in your pre-tokenization step. in transcripts sometimes words get duplicated; see the repeated 'the the' pattern. that can cause token explosion and cost.
[06:48] Tom: ah yes we have some legacy template code that concatenates in a naive way. so that could be the source.
[06:53] Lena: worth normalizing that. next i want to demo correlation across requests — Console has a session view. i'll filter by session id, and you can see all requests, retries, and their outcomes. this is useful for multi-turn flows.
[07:12] Priya: when you show session, is user PII masked?
[07:18] Lena: default in hosted is masked, but in Private you control masking. in pilot we'll propose an encrypted stream into your VPC with only telemetry exported to Redwood console.
[07:30] Samir: quick pause — any immediate blockers from a security/compliance POV?
[07:33] Priya: we'd want to see a network diagram and the KMS integration details before we can proceed. also need to know retention windows for replay payloads.
[07:40] Samir: noted and i'll share that.
[07:43] --- deeper troubleshooting ---
[08:00] Lena: ok switching to error analysis — Console tags error classes (e.g., 5xx-runtime, 4xx-input, kv-miss). i'm opening a sample 500, you can see the stack map and the token index where it fails. there's also a small note where the model returned an unusual decoding token which then triggered the runtime guardrail. sometimes that points back to tokenizer mismatch.
[08:28] Tom: tokenizer mismatch — we used a legacy tokenizer from an upstream library, could cause misaligned token ids.
[08:35] Lena: yep, Console has a tokenizer diff tool. i'll run it quickly — it'll show differing token lengths and the mapping. see here, the input that should be 12 tokens is 22 tokens under legacy tokenizer. that explains both cost and TTL of KV keys.
[08:55] Ethan: wow that's helpful. how easy is it to swap tokenizers in our preproc pipeline?
[08:59] Priya: depends on codebase, but we can add an adapter layer to canonicalize to the studio tokenizer.
[09:06] Lena: also note we have a lightweight SDK helper to normalize templates pre-send. small change usually reduces token churn.
[09:12] Samir: ok, on the operational side — for the pilot we'd recommend: 1) instrument a small set of endpoints, 2) route those to Dedicated pool, 3) enable full tracing for 48h to capture patterns, 4) run replay harness on known failures.
[09:30] Tom: that seems reasonable. cost-wise what's the expectation for a two-week pilot?
[09:35] Samir: it depends on request volume; rough back-of-envelope for 100k tokens/day mid-range model is X dollars; i'll send a tailored estimate after we see sample traces.
[09:45] Priya: for running replay agent in our infra, is there a minimal permissions list?
[09:50] Lena: yes, replay-agent needs permissions to pull model weights if you pin models on-prem, but if you route to Redwood hosted it only needs egress to Redwood endpoints. more detail in the agent readme.
[09:58] --- timestamps skip ahead, demo continues ---
[15:02] Lena: now showing the topological map — this is where traces map across services (preproc -> tokenization -> runtime -> response postproc). when you click a node it surfaces sample spans and the percentile latency. you can then open a request timeline with token-by-token times.
[20:05] Tom: can we export those timelines as CSV for our analysis?
[20:10] Lena: yes export button top-right. CSV contains span start/end, token index, and metadata (obfuscated if needed).
[24:21] Ethan: in the event of an incident, can we create a runbook entry directly from the Console?
[24:26] Samir: yes, there's an 'Create incident' that ties a trace, related alerts, and a snapshot of related configuration. you can then assign to on-call with links into your pager system.
[28:40] Priya: one more on security — what's the retention if we choose "short-term" telemetry?
[28:45] Samir: retention tiers are 7/30/90 days for telemetry; full payloads are optional and can be set to 0-30 days depending on agreement.
[29:00] Lena: demo wrap — i'll now show how to add a custom metric. click 'Create metric' -> define filter (e.g., route == /chat AND kv_miss == true) -> aggregation P95 -> then you can attach alert policies.
[29:25] Tom: that will help us detect when prefix churn spikes.
[29:30] Lena: exactly.
[35:12] Ethan: moving to pilot scope — what do you need from us to get started?
[35:17] Samir: sample traces (Tom), decision on Dedicated vs Private (Priya), and legal/compliance kickoff to sign pilot paperwork (Ethan). we'll aim for a kickoff week of Aug 10 if timelines align.
[35:33] Priya: legal will need the SOC2 docs and network diagram, also a summary of data flows.
[35:40] Samir: will send that by Aug 2.
[35:45] Tom: quick technical: can the Console tie traces to our internal request IDs so we can cross-reference logs?
[35:50] Lena: yes, there's a correlation key you can pass with the request header. Console will index it and allow you to jump into your logs via a hyperlink if you configure the log-stitching endpoint.
[36:05] Tom: nice. that will make root cause much faster.
[40:00] --- wrap up / recap ---
[40:10] Samir: recap: Lena will run a 1-hour replay benchmark against provided traces; Tom will upload anonymized traces and confirm SLOs; i will send security and pricing; Ethan will confirm pilot stakeholders. we'll schedule POC kickoff for week of Aug 10.
[40:30] Ethan: let's aim for Aug 11 14:00 UTC tentatively.
[40:35] Samir: works for us.
[40:40] Priya: thanks everyone — this was useful.
[40:45] Tom: thanks, appreciate the walkthrough.
[40:50] Lena: thanks all — i'll follow up with the replay results and a short playbook PDF.
[41:00] --- meeting ended ---

Notes on transcription quirks: occasional mis-heard product words (e.g., "replay agent" transcribed as "replay age end"), speaker label sometimes interchanges AE/SE. there are filler words and short crosstalks that may not be perfectly captured.
